channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Bans Unapproved Meetings for School Directors
item.description: Uzbekistan's Deputy Prime Minister for Education, Erkinjon Turdimov, announced a ban on summoning school directors to meetings without prior ministry approval. He emphasized that school leaders should focus on their primary duties rather than attending numerous unscheduled gatherings. Turdimov stated that any required meeting must be approved by the ministry, and school principals should not be called to local government sessions.

item.title: Afghan Traders' Goods at Risk of Auction in Pakistan Amid Taliban Policies
item.description: Documents reveal that over 140 containers belonging to approximately 19 Afghan trading companies face auction at Pakistan's Karachi port. Pakistan Customs has issued notices warning of auction if goods are not cleared by the deadline. The threatened goods include sugar, oils, infant formula, and raw materials. A Taliban commercial attaché requested intervention, as container fees and penalties reportedly exceed the goods' value.

item.title: Pakistan's Ex-Envoy Worried by Taliban's Growing Ties with Russia and India
item.description: Former Pakistani special representative Asif Durrani expressed concern over the Taliban's strengthening alliance with Russia and India, viewing it as detrimental to Pakistan's interests. He stated that this convergence reduces the Taliban's responsiveness to Pakistan's security concerns, noting that the Taliban have historically been unaccountable to Pakistan on such matters. Durrani also highlighted the expanding list of countries supporting the Taliban, including Qatar, Turkey, Iran, and Central Asian republics.

item.title: US CENTCOM Commander Visits Strait of Hormuz, Claims Clear Waterways
item.description: CENTCOM Commander Brad Cooper visited the Strait of Hormuz, flying over the waterway and meeting with personnel involved in clearing naval mines. He stated that Iranian naval mines have been cleared from key transit routes, asserting US and partner control over the international waterway. CENTCOM claims over 3,000 ships have successfully transited the strait in the last six months.

item.title: Afghanistan Earthquake Felt in Three Regions of Uzbekistan
item.description: An earthquake that occurred in Afghanistan on the evening of October 25 was felt in several regions of Uzbekistan. The tremors were registered with a magnitude of 2 in the Surxondaryo, Fergana, and Kashkadaryo provinces. The epicenter was the city of Badakhshan, located 577 km southeast of Tashkent, at a depth of 149 km.

item.title: Iran Claims Downing US LUCAS Drone Over Bandar Abbas
item.description: Iranian military officials announced they shot down a US LUCAS drone over the port city of Bandar Abbas. According to an Iranian general, the US developed this drone based on Iran's Shahed-136 model. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Two Pakistani Soldiers Killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Operation
item.description: The Pakistani army reported that two soldiers were killed during an operation against Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) elements in Dera Ismail Khan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Six militants were also killed. The army claims these individuals were involved in terrorist acts and the killing of civilians. Weapons and ammunition were seized.

item.title: Tehran Hosts Diplomatic Rush Amidst US and Israeli Election Cycles
item.description: Tehran has become a hub for diplomatic activity with visits from Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Pakistan's Army Chief Asim Munir. The meetings focused on de-escalating the volatile Middle East situation, with blame for the current precarious state attributed to the US, Israel, and Iran. The diplomatic surge raises questions about its effectiveness in preventing further conflict.

item.title: Ekibastuz GRES-1 fined for environmental pollution from ash and slag waste
item.description: Pavlodar environmental prosecutor's office discovered environmental pollution from ash and slag waste near Ekibastuz GRES-1 due to a leak. The enterprise was fined 500 MCI (2,162,500 tenge) by the Ekibastuz City Court for violating environmental laws. Another fine of approximately 70 million tenge was issued for exceeding atmospheric emission limits.

item.title: Kazakhstan opens its 300th voluntary fire post in Karaganda region
item.description: The 300th voluntary fire post has been opened in the village of Ospen, Shetsky district, Karaganda region, according to the Ministry of Emergency Situations of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The post, built from prefabricated structures, will serve four settlements with over 1,400 residents. It is equipped with a fire truck and radio communication systems.

item.title: Israel Displaces Over 2,600 Palestinians in Hebron, Palestinian PM's Office Reports
item.description: The Palestinian Prime Minister's office stated that Israeli forces have forcibly displaced 2,670 Palestinians from their homes in Hebron, West Bank. The majority of those displaced are women, children, and the elderly. This action follows the killing of two Israeli soldiers in Hebron. The Palestinian Authority condemned the operation as 'collective punishment'.

item.title: Qatar Mediators in Tehran Amidst US Threats of Further Strikes on Iran
item.description: Qatari mediators arrived in Tehran as US President Donald Trump threatened further strikes against Iran. An Iranian official stated the visit is part of routine message exchanges amid heightened tensions. The official cited US refusal to accept Iran's demands and repeated breaches of commitments as the main obstacle to a diplomatic solution. Iran's Parliament Speaker vowed a response to any violation of its territorial integrity.

item.title: Pakistan Auctions Hundreds of Containers Belonging to Afghan Traders Amid Trade Disruptions
item.description: Pakistan's Karachi Port customs authority is auctioning hundreds of containers carrying goods from Afghan traders due to unpaid taxes and charges. Images show goods being offered for sale. Afghanistan's Chamber of Commerce deems this a violation of trade laws. The move occurs amid political tensions and border closures, which have drastically reduced bilateral trade by 95% compared to the previous fiscal year.

item.title: Man's Second Wife Murders His Wife and Six-Year-Old Daughter in Sirdaryo
item.description: In Sirdaryo, a man's second wife fatally stabbed his wife and their six-year-old daughter. The 29-year-old woman is responsible for two deaths and seriously injured another three-year-old daughter. The motive for the attack is currently under investigation.

item.title: Experts Cite Economic Hardship and Restrictions for Declining Male University Enrollment in Afghanistan
item.description: Experts attribute the decline in male university enrollment in Afghanistan to economic hardship, social pressure, and educational restrictions. Factors include imposed viewpoints, dress codes, and a lack of academic freedom. Students seek quality education, job opportunities, and a conducive learning environment.

item.title: Protests held across Europe demanding housing, pension, and education reforms
item.description: Hundreds of thousands protested in France, with demonstrations also occurring in Italy, Portugal, Spain, Belgium, and Albania. Protesters demanded measures to reduce the cost of living, maintain public service funding, and change social policies. Clashes with police were reported in several French cities, leading to over 1,300 arrests. Security forces used tear gas and water cannons. 53 security personnel were injured.

item.title: Taliban Reportedly Suspend Government Employee Salaries Until Further Notice
item.description: Sources within Taliban-controlled government departments report that salary payments for civil and military employees have been suspended until further notice. The Ministry of Finance has delayed salary disbursements, with the reasons remaining unclear. This delay causes hardship amid approaching winter.

item.title: Israel Demolishes Entire Palestinian Neighborhood in Hebron, Displacing 1,500
item.description: Israeli forces are demolishing residential buildings in the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank. This action follows an attack on an Israeli military checkpoint. The demolition has left approximately 1,500 Palestinians homeless.

item.title: UN: Restrictions on women and interference disrupt humanitarian aid in Afghanistan
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reports that restrictions on female staff and interference in aid operations are hindering humanitarian assistance in Afghanistan. While reported incidents decreased in September, this may not reflect an improvement. OCHA noted that administrative and programmatic interference, along with restrictions affecting female aid workers and recipients, are key factors.

item.title: Taliban Leader Approves Merger of Kabul Bank with Bank Millie Afghan
item.description: Taliban Supreme Leader Hibatullah Akhundzada has approved the merger of Kabul Bank with the Taliban-controlled Bank-e-Millie Afghan (BMA). Documents reveal Kabul Bank faces severe system challenges, with Oracle rejecting software upgrades. Storage devices are nearing end-of-life, and a strategic plan decision is postponed due to the merger.

item.title: Kazakh Wrestlers Win First World Championship Medals in Astana
item.description: Kazakh Greco-Roman wrestlers Iskhar Kurbaev and Aidoss Sultangali secured bronze medals at the World Wrestling Championships held in Astana. These are the first medals for Kazakhstan at their home world championship. Kurbaev won his bronze medal match in the 55kg category by technical fall, while Sultangali claimed bronze in the 60kg category.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Egypt strengthen cooperation in the agricultural sector
item.description: Uzbekistan and Egypt are enhancing collaboration in agriculture, focusing on food security and modern technologies. A meeting between Uzbek Ministry of Economy and Finance and an Egyptian agricultural research delegation discussed joint initiatives in farming, livestock, and veterinary science. A memorandum of cooperation was signed.

item.title: Former heads of two Tashkent tax inspectorates sentenced for corruption
item.description: Former heads of the tax inspectorates in Tashkent's Mirzo Ulugbek and Shaykhontohur districts have been found guilty of abuse of power and other crimes. One official demanded money from an entrepreneur, while the other was involved in violations related to tax operations amounting to 22.7 billion soums.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Expand Cooperation in Coal Field Development
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkey are set to enhance cooperation in developing the country's coal resources. Officials from Uzbekistan's Ministry of Mining Industry and Geology met with the regional head of Turkey's Cengiz Holding to discuss investment projects and the geological exploration of promising coal deposits in the Surkhandarya and Tashkent regions. This collaboration aims to boost foreign investment and develop new projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan proposes SCO countries exchange water-saving technologies
item.description: Kazakhstan has proposed creating a regional platform for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) countries to exchange water-saving agricultural technologies and expertise. The initiative aims to promote drip and sprinkler irrigation, digital soil moisture control, and automated watering systems. Kazakhstan plans to increase irrigated land using these technologies by 2030.

item.title: New Plant Launched in Kentau City, Turkistan Region
item.description: A new plant producing industrial metal structures and products has started operations in the industrial zone of Kentau city, Turkistan region. The opening ceremony was attended by the region's governor, Nuralhan Kosherov. The project, attracting 1.5 billion tenge in investment, created 30 new jobs and has an annual production capacity of 100 units.

item.title: Uzbekistan Athletes Achieve Third Place at Para Asian Games in Japan
item.description: Uzbekistan's national team secured third place overall at the V Summer Para Asian Games in Japan, winning 45 gold, 49 silver, and 51 bronze medals. President Mirziyoyev congratulated the athletes, highlighting their achievements, including new world and Asian records set by powerlifter Ro'za Qo'ziyeva and others.

item.title: Obama Criticizes Trump Administration on Iran War, Inflation, and White House Renovation
item.description: Former US President Barack Obama criticized the Trump administration's policies on the Iran war, rising inflation, and the White House renovation project during a campaign rally. He urged voters to use the upcoming midterm elections to curb "foolish actions" of the current administration.

item.title: Early Parliamentary Elections Held in Serbia Amid Student Protests Against Vučić
item.description: Serbia is holding early parliamentary elections, with results determining President Vučić's ability to retain power after years of leadership. Critics accuse him of corruption and ties to organized crime. The elections occur amidst heightened tensions and accusations of voter intimidation.

item.title: Taliban Arrest Four Residents in Panjshir's Dara District
item.description: The Taliban have arrested four residents from the Dara district of Panjshir province. The specific reasons for the arrests and the current whereabouts of the individuals were not immediately clear from the report.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Congratulates Asian Para Games Winners and Participants
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated the winners and participants of the Asian Para Games. He highly praised the athletes' courage and resilience, expressing gratitude to their parents and coaches. Uzbekistan's delegation secured a top-three finish with 145 medals at the competition in Japan.

item.title: Uzbek doctors successfully perform complex brain aneurysm stenting procedure independently
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Medical Center reports its interventional radiologists have independently performed a complex brain aneurysm stenting procedure for the first time. Previously, such high-tech operations often required foreign specialists. A 55-year-old patient with dizziness and vision problems underwent the minimally invasive procedure, which avoids skull trepanation and speeds recovery.

item.title: Israelis protest Netanyahu government, demand accountability for October 7 Hamas attack
item.description: Citizens in Israel have taken to the streets to protest the Netanyahu government. Protesters are demanding accountability for the government's alleged failure to prevent the October 7 Hamas attack. The protests highlight ongoing public discontent with the current administration's handling of security matters.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Save Up to 2.2 Billion Cubic Meters of Water Annually
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to expand water-saving technologies to 1.3 million hectares by 2030, potentially saving up to 2.2 billion cubic meters of irrigation water per year. The government has increased compensation for farmers adopting these technologies and is proposing a joint platform for water-saving technology exchange within the SCO.

item.title: Kunduz Gold Mine Begins Operations with $20 Million Investment
item.description: Gold mining operations have commenced in Afghanistan's Kunduz province with a $20 million investment in the Qala-e-Zal district. Local authorities describe it as one of Kunduz's largest mining projects, expected to create hundreds of jobs and boost economic development. The contracting company will also fund road construction and other development projects in the district.

item.title: Lisbon Police Disperse Protest Camp Amid Housing Crisis
item.description: Lisbon police forcibly dispersed a protest camp set up by demonstrators against rising housing costs in Rossio Square. Clashes occurred, resulting in arrests and injuries. Thousands had marched demanding affordable housing, subsequently setting up over 100 tents. A local politician criticized the police action as excessive.

item.title: Kazakhstan Celebrates Republic Day After 13-Year Hiatus
item.description: Kazakhstan is celebrating Republic Day on October 25, a national holiday marked by cultural and sporting events. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated Kazakhstan has become a respected, influential middle power. This is the fifth time Republic Day is celebrated since its re-establishment in 2022.

item.title: US Wheat Prices Decline While Kazakhstan Experiences Low Trade Volume
item.description: Wheat prices are falling in the United States, coinciding with a period of minimal trading activity in Kazakhstan. This situation indicates a potential shift in global grain markets, with implications for both exporting and importing nations. The reasons for the low trade volume in Kazakhstan are not specified.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Qatar Discuss Opening Direct Flights
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Qatar held discussions on opening direct flights during a working visit by Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Daniyar Aman-geldyev, to Qatar. Both sides emphasized that direct air travel would boost trade, business contacts, tourism, and economic ties. They also discussed holding the second session of the Kyrgyz-Qatari Joint Intergovernmental Commission.

item.title: Elena Rybakina Wins Second Consecutive Ningbo Open Title
item.description: Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina successfully defended her title at the WTA 500 Ningbo Open, defeating Canada's Leylah Fernandez 6-2, 6-2 in the final. This marks her second consecutive victory at the tournament. Rybakina previously beat Polina Kudermetova, Katarzyna Kawa, and Diana Shnaider en route to the final. Her next tournament is in Tokyo.
